workouts.title: Before Photos
workouts.description: Taking "Before Pictures" will allow you to clearly see where you are starting your shoulder mobility journey from. Ideally, you want to reveal as much as your shoulder and upper body area as possible in the pictures. For that reason, men are encouraged to take their photos topless or in a tank top and women in sports bra or tank top. 1. Picture should be taken up to the chin with the full arm in view. 2. Stand naturally with arms loose and relaxed by your sides. 1. Picture should be taken from the top of the head to the the waist. 2. Stand naturally with arms loose and relaxed by your sides.

workouts.title: ShoulderROM Pre-Test
workouts.description: Ensure you have your ShoulderROM Scorecard printed to document your results. Keep a phone or camera handy to capture your before photos and even video your tests for reference and review. We also recommend taking regular photos to track any visible improvements in your shoulder area. Remember we'll be grading each test out of 3. Grade '0' if there is any pain whatsoever in the movement (pain) Grade '1' if the range is very restricted (difficulty moving) Grade '2' if range is mildly restricted (movement a little difficult) Grade '3' if you can exhibit a full range of motion (Nothing limiting movement)

sections.name: POST TEST PHOTOS

items.movement: Next, find your ShoulderROM Score Card from Week 1 and as you go through the 5 tests, self grade each test out of 3.
Grade '0' if there is any pain whatsoever in the movement (pain)
Grade '1' if the range is very restricted (difficulty moving)
Grade '2' if range is mildly restricted (movement a little difficult)
Grade '3' if you can exhibit a full range of motion (Nothing limiting movement)

sections.format: To start, take your "After" ShoulderROM pictures so you can compare your shoulder changes from week 1 to week 8. Aim to take these photos the same way you did for your pre test -- Wearing the same clothes, in front of the same wall, taken from the same height and angle... all of those little factors will help make it easier to see the changes in your pictures.

workouts.title: ShoulderROM Analysis
workouts.description: At the end of the test, add up your score and compare to Week 1. Review your videos from each movement and compare. What do you notice when you compare the two sets of videos? Do you see an improvement in range, shoulder positioning? Do you feel less limitation or pain? What is your biggest take away after completing ShoulderROM ?

workouts.title: The ShoulderROM Philosophy
workouts.description: We'll incorporate 3 different approaches into each ShoulderROM session to better improve shoulder flexibility, stability and strength. 1. Soft Tissue Work Each session will begin with some foam roller / lacrosse ball work to help increase the effectiveness of the session. This work is like adding water to brittle clay and will prep your soft tissue for the work ahead. 2. Dynamic Stretching Allows us to rewire the brain and demonstrate that we can safely go to these new ranges of motion. 3. Strengthen Good Positions Now that we've increased our range, we need to let our body know that it's okay to be stronger in these new positions.

workouts.title: Shoulder Pain
workouts.description: Although the shoulders are the most flexible joint in the body here are some underlying factors that could be leading to our shoulder becoming still and painful. 1. Too Much Sitting We are wired to move and sitting for long periods can have a negative effect on our bodies. Moving frequently and sitting with better posture are some ways to combat those negative effects. 2. Lack of Core Stability If our foundation is weak everything else will be too. We'll do some work with it in this program but if you feel you need additional core focus, check out our Functional Core program. It was designed to improve core stability and can be done in conjunction with this program. 3. Lack of Shoulder Stability If we are lacking proper strength and stability in our shoulders, we won't be able to express full power until our body knows it can do that safely. 4. Move Small Our shoulder is meant to move through a full 360 degree range. In this day and age, many adults can go long periods without moving their shoulders through big ranges of motion as they were intended. We'll work to rectify every time you do a ShoulderROM workout.
